global_read: global.json (11:39) shows Brent at $96.29 (+2.36% 1d, +24.92% 1mo) and WTI $88.25 (+1.64% 1d, +20.54% 1mo) -- both grinding to fresh highs on a genuine THIRD straight day of oil escalation, distinct from the whipsaw/ceasefire-hope pullback pattern seen mid-month. Equities/vol stayed calm globally (S&P -0.14% 1d, Dow -0.01% 1d, VIX actually down -2.4% 1d to 16.64) -- global risk appetite is still shrugging this off on the surface. PKR/USD 277.57 (+0.02% 1d, +0.26% 1mo) and DXY 100.99 (-0.15% 1d) remain calm, the rupee has not cracked yet. Gold -0.55% 1d is not showing a classic flight-to-safety bid either. Net read: global risk tape looks deceptively benign, but it is not pricing the same oil-supply-shock risk this desk's domestic/geo lens is tracking -- PSX has repeatedly sold off hard on Hormuz/Red Sea escalation headlines even on days global indices stayed flat, so global calm should not be read as a green light for PSX today.
drivers: NEW this run: Houthis carried out their first-ever DIRECT attack on tankers in this escalation cycle, striking two Saudi-flagged/linked vessels (Encelia and Layla) off Al Shuqaiq on Saudi Arabia's Red Sea coast on 2026-07-22, after declaring a maritime blockade of Saudi Red Sea ports on 2026-07-20 -- a qualitatively new escalation vector (Red Sea/Bab-al-Mandab, not just Hormuz) threatening up to ~4mn bpd of redirected Saudi crude exports (https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2026-07-22/brent-crude-spikes-in-late-trading-after-red-sea-tanker-attack, https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2026/7/22/yemens-houthis-claim-attack-on-two-saudi-oil-tankers, https://oilprice.com/Energy/Oil-Prices/Houthi-Red-Sea-Blockade-Could-Shatter-Hopes-for-Lower-Oil-Prices.html)

Brent has now risen for three straight sessions to $96.29 (+2.36% 1d, +24.92% 1mo per global.json 11:39) -- unlike the mid-July pattern of intraday spikes followed by ceasefire-hope pullbacks, this move has held and extended, which changes the read from 'noisy headline risk' to 'sustained supply-shock repricing' (global.json)

Company-specific, not macro, but logged for completeness: BWCL (Bestway Cement) reported 9MFY26 profit of Rs17.91bn (+2% YoY, not the +7% figure in today's Sentinel flag) with EPS Rs30.04 and a Rs10/share dividend already declared for that nine-month period -- gross profit actually fell 18% YoY on rising input costs, with the bottom-line gain driven by associate income and debt-servicing savings rather than core operations; flagging the +2%-vs-+7% discrepancy for Strategist/Auditor to reconcile against the primary PSX filing before sizing any BWCL-specific setup (https://mettisglobal.news/BWCL-9MFY26-profit-inches-up-2-59750)

Net regime read: this is not the familiar headline-spike-then-fade pattern -- a genuinely new escalation vector (direct Houthi tanker strikes, Saudi Red Sea blockade) has driven THREE straight days of Brent gains to a fresh $96+ high, domestic T-bill yields were already re-pricing the prior week's escalation before this print, the SBP MPC lands in 4 days with reserves unverified past 07-10, and global equity/VIX calm has repeatedly proven a poor predictor of PSX's own reaction to these specific headlines.
